items.text: Street, Inside the City

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: Previously, we were at ...

items.speaker: Citizen VI
items.text: Lùshǔ the Xiángruì came to the human world to go through the god's test, but she repented!

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: Exactly. She had been troubled by the repentance until the New Year's Eve. That night, her tutor straightened her out, and she was very grateful. After that, she bid him goodbye and went to the broken bridge alone.

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: However, ladies and gentlemen, the Shuòrì this year happened to be the beginning of spring. Such a coincidence happens only once every 100 years. On this peculiar day, the thunderstorm was raging, and all the strangest things happened!

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: The cliff was shrouded in confusing fog, and below was a bottomless abyss! No one had ever jumped over the bridge successfully, yet the Lùshǔ decided to make an attempt, for the sake of the people who believed in her! She was determined to retrieve the tortoise shell divination ...

items.speaker: Citizen VI
items.text: That's not it! She used the wooden chip! Not the tortoise shell!

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: Emm ...

items.speaker: Citizen II
items.text: You've told this story for many times, and still getting it wrong? You have to admit you're not young anymore.

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: Well, there is no such thing as a perfect story. Adaptations are always allowed, right? Please pretend you didn't hear me and forget about it ...

items.speaker: Citizen VII
items.text: Give me a break. He's telling that story again? I thought he'd be done with it after last time. I even bought a ticket!

items.speaker: Citizen V
items.text: "Last time"? When, last year? Did you sleep for a whole year?

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: I hear you, gentleman in blue.

items.speaker: Citizen VII
items.text: Now he's listening ...

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: You know, you're part of the story, just like me.

items.speaker: Citizen VII
items.text: Me? What do you mean?

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: Listen and you'll know. So the Lùshǔ jumped over the bridge, awakened the Yuān Temple, and revived the Pèilín River. As a result, more and more people come to the Pèi City at festivals, so I start telling stories again.

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: As for you ...

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: The Lùshǔ took over your tavern and turned you into her kind because you were an unscrupulous profiteer. You gave short weight to the people. That caused the decline of your business, yet you blamed it on the poor harvest.

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: But I think the Lùshǔ saved you from the plight! She ran the tavern for you, and you had a good sleep during that time. In a word, you did nothing good, but things ended up well for you!

items.speaker: Citizen VI
items.text: What? No way!

items.speaker: Citizen VI
items.text: I want that, too. If only somebody could finish my essay when I fall asleep!

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: Already writing a political essay at this age? You have a promising future, young man ...

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: But I think you should go home now and get some sleep. You need to rest well, so you can continue with your studies tomorrow.

items.speaker: Storyteller
items.text: After all, the essay matters much more than the story, right?
Amidst the festive hustle and bustle, a farewell brews in front of the city gates.
This is the place from which people come, and people go.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: I have so many things to write about this time, enough for me to write a travel note.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: What should I call it? Travel in the East? Journey to Pèi City?

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Neither of them sounds good.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: There are already too many Travels and Journeys. I think you are different from those authors, Madam, so ...
Gětiān escorts the group to a spot near the city gate, where the road splits into two. On one side lies the road up the mountain, and on the other lies the road down.
He slowly descends to the ground, standing still, stiff and slightly uncomfortable.
The human companions of the two arcanists retreat in caution and fear from the strange bird creature.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Indeed. Unlike others, the two of you have experienced it in its entirety.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: What do you mean?

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: There was a beginning, and now here is an end. Forget not where you came from at the end—this is entirety.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Thus, happiness is found.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: I'm sorry that I still don't understand your riddles.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: That's no matter.

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: Emm ... Sorry to interrupt you. Can we go? I really want to go home right away ...

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Ah, then we shall ...

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Please wait. There's one more thing.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Certainly, please.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: The questions you asked—have you had the answers?

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: I'm not sure.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: What do you mean?

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: When Jiǔ Niángzǐ jumped over the bridge, Yenisei saw a pattern being formed where I wrote my question.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: We didn't understand it. It didn't bother us either, perhaps because there was no answer to my question ...

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: A question is asked, and a divination is made. What you saw might be a Hexagram, not the interpretation of it.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Do you still remember what it looks like?
Yenisei thinks for a moment and uses a rock hammer handle to draw crooked and twisted lines in the sand, with occasional breaks in the middle of them.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: It changed a little ... and ended up like this.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: The Hexagram of Water and Fire.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: I'd assume this belongs to an elderly person. What about yours?
Yenisei is stunned for a moment, then draws a few more lines. By the end of it, her offering is already rather messy, so much so that she stretches out a section of it.
Fortunately, Gětiān can still read it.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: This is ... Xū, the Hexagram of waiting. Though I don't know what could be derived from it ...

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: The interpretation is simple. Above is Water, the stranding dragon, advising patience. Below is uprightness, which means you will smooth away the obstacles.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Which means ...?

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: You will find your water. All you need to do is wait.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Yes, thank you. I didn't know that.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: As for your Hexagram ...

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: You have gone across the river. A decision has been made.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Turns out The Divination doesn't help at all.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: It does, if you believe in it.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: No. I know what you mean.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: It is exactly how I expected it to be. Thank you, Mr. Gětiān.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: No need.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: And what about you? Have you learned your answer?

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: It told me to let things be.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: Since I have left the mountain ... I should follow what's inside my mind.
Gětiān turns his head and points his wings toward the path up the mountain.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: I remember that at the end of the Pèilín River, where the lanterns float, stands a great building.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: It might be real or illusional. I have seen it many times, yet I have never thought of going there.
The two of them look in the direction pointed out by Gětiān, only seeing the jungle into which Jiǔ Niángzǐ disappeared, and nothing more.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: There's nothing there.

items.speaker: Getian
items.text: I will go anyway.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Then ...

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: What about Jiǔ Niángzǐ? She jumped over the bridge. Is she never coming back?
Gětiān doesn't answer, he only shakes his head. All Yenisei can do is glance over to Gětiān filled with unspoken inquiries.
Bessmert turns toward the distant cliffs and jungle, standing without speaking for a long while.
Until at last she breaks her silence.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Perhaps ...

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Perhaps we will meet again one day.
